title: Draft: Thrift: Reassemble nested structures
description:
- Make sure reassembly requests & errors are properly propagated from
  any point in the PDU, no matter how many sub-structure levels.
- Handle the sub-dissection methods as well:
  - Ensure the sub-dissection methods handle errors from previous calls.
  - Reduce the error handling needed in sub-dissector implementations.
  - Add missing sub-dissection methods for list, set, and map.
  - Add the handling of sub-structure.

Additional changes:
- Use of constants instead of hard-coded values.
- Removed U64 support (never supported by thrift code generator, only
  referenced in the C++ thrift library header but not supported in reality.
- Removed references to UTF-8 and UTF-16 string for the same reason.
- Replaced references to UTF-7 string with just string (same reason).
- Replaced references to byte with i8 as the documentation explicitly
  states that byte is a compatibility name.

Documentation reference:
- https://thrift.apache.org/developers
- https://thrift.apache.org/docs/idl.html
- https://erikvanoosten.github.io/thrift-missing-specification/
- https://diwakergupta.github.io/thrift-missing-guide/

Closes #16244

notes.body:
I have a few remarks regarding this MR:
1. This is only the first part as I am currently working on the merge with TCompactProtocol in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3171 (I’ll take care of the rebase with the complete proposal).
2. Since I am currently using the same conventions to update the TCompactProtocol part, the sooner I have remarks, the faster it will be taken into account.
3. Regarding the 3 commits, the question is what can be squashed in and what should be in a different MR?

Hi,
No real preference but would it make sense to commit the compact protocol MR first and then
amend it? Having one huge MR might make it hard to review. Adding unrelated stuff in one MR might confuse things?
The slogan on this MR is a bit misleading isn't it?
Regards
Anders

I'll reword the MR (this one contains the fix on basic dissection as well as sub-dissection but also the completion of sub-dissection so it's already slightly misleading).

The complete version will handle everything properly (I hope ^__^):
- TBinaryProtocol basic dissection
- TCompactProtocol basic dissection
- TBinaryProtocol sub-dissection
- TCompactProtocol sub-dissection
- Reassembly in TCP for all of the above
- Heuristic dissector for TCP, UDP, and USB bulk for both variants.

In any case, since most of the compact handling will rewritten/rearranged to handle sub-dissection and reassembly, I think it will be easier to review the new code than the changes.

In any case, I'm completely fine with the merge of !3171 to allow everyone to test this part and if any problem is found, I'll make sure I test the case with the final MR.

I'm still thinking about some details on the handling of sub-dissection to make it easier to use with both binary and compact variants so it will take some time.

As discussed in !3171, the current implementation shows structure fields in the following way:
```text
- Struct
  - Type: T_I32 (0x08)
  - Field Id: 1
  - Integer32: 42
  - Type: T_BINARY (0x0b)
  - Field Id: 2
  - Length: 42
  - String: Requested power exceeds device's tolerance
  - Type: T_STRUCT (0x0c)
  - Field Id: 42
  + Struct
  - Type: T_STOP
```
This display ensures a reasonable number of sub-tree levels (low horizontal expansion) to the expense of being difficult to read when a structure has a lot of sub-fields (high vertical expansion).

On the other hand, the proposed implementation for compact protocol shows something like that (adjusted for compact specificities):
```text
- Struct
  - Member 1
    - .... 0101 Type: T_I32 (0x05)
    - 0001 .... Field Id Delta: 1
    - [Field Id: 1]
    - Integer32: 42
  - Member 2
    - .... 1000 Type: T_BINARY (0x08)
    - 0001 .... Field Id Delta: 1
    - [Field Id: 2]
    - Length: 42
    - String: Requested power exceeds device's tolerance
  - Member 3
    - .... 1000 Type: T_STRUCT (0x0c)
    - Field Id: 42
    + Struct
```
This display increases the number of sub-tree to increase the readability of the fields (higher horizontal expansion but lower vertical if we don't expand everything).

It might be possible to increase the readability without adding as much width as with the TCompact proposal using something like this.
```text
- Struct
  - Field Header: 1 # TBinaryProtocol version
    - Type: T_I32 (0x08)
    - Field Id: 1
  - Integer32: 42
  - Field Header: 2 # TCompactProtocol version
    - .... 1000 Type: T_BINARY (0x08)
    - 0001 .... Field Id Delta: 1
    - [Field Id: 2]
    - Length: 42
  - String: Requested power exceeds device's tolerance
  + Field Header: 42 # Collapsed
  + Struct
```

And for sub-dissectors, we would still have the choice of activating the internal thrift fields in the same way:
```text
- Invalid Parameter Error
  - Field Header: 1
    - Type: T_I32 (0x08)
    - Field Id: 1
  - Generic Error Code: Parameter value out of range (42)
  - Field Header: 2
    - .... 1000 Type: T_BINARY (0x08)
    - 0001 .... Field Id Delta: 1
    - [Field Id: 2]
    - Length: 42
  - Error description: Requested power exceeds device's tolerance
  + Field Header: 42 # Collapsed
  + Power range
```
or not:
```text
- Invalid Parameter Error
  - Generic Error Code: Parameter value out of range (42)
  - Error description: Requested power exceeds device's tolerance
  + Power range
```
This way, we would clearly see the field number (which is the important part when we don't have a specific dissector and are using baseline Wireshark with the Thrift-generated HTML documentation next to it) and the value without having to expand sub-tree).

Any comment welcome. Before I start going that way, I still need to finish the merge with sub-dissection support so there is time.

I edited my previous comment regarding the last proposal: specific field description elements are also pushed into the field header sub-tree for readability:
- String/binary’s length.
- ~~List/set’s type of elements and length.~~
- ~~Map’s types of key and value, and length.~~

It will also be more consistent as we will always see the same pattern:
```text
- Struct
  + Field Header
  + Field Value
  + Field Header
  + Field Value
  ...
```
Whatever the value is (either direct value or sub-tree for struct and containers).
I’ll also try to put some useful info in the title for the field header as it was done in the initial compact proposal, it seems relatively easy with the way I structured it.

Edit: First tries lead me to think it might become confusing in case we have several level of encapsulation, I’ll see how I do that to keep it clear…

Edit 2: Only binary/string length will go into the Field header if available. Lists, sets, and maps create a subtree anyway so the few elements at the beginning of this sub-tree do not impact readability.
Closing MR as it will be replaced with the complete binary+compact+sub-dissection.

commits_data.message:
Thrift: Reassemble nested structures

- Make sure reassembly requests & errors are properly propagated from
  any point in the PDU, no matter how many sub-structure levels.
- Handle the sub-dissection methods as well:
